name: Fast Image Cache
baseline: Loading individual JPEG files with UIImage(contentsOfFile:) and letting Core Animation decode them on the main thread
verdict_reason: Path's demo measured ~59 FPS against ~35 FPS while scrolling, but on the iOS 7 platform the README describes, where third-party apps got only a software JPEG decoder and no background-decoding API. Current iOS offers UIImage.preparingForDisplay() and ImageIO thumbnails, and the library has had no commits since 2016, so the baseline it beat is no longer today's.
tier_reason: First-party demo app in the repository; device, OS version and build configuration are not stated.
claimed_speedup: Scrolling ~59FPS vs ~35FPS for the conventional method; extra memory 0.09MB vs 1.34MB above baseline; at the cost of 2.2MB vs 568KB on disk.
workload: Scrolling a table of JPEG thumbnails in the bundled demo app; RPRVT measured for one screen of thumbnails.
one_liner: Stores pre-decoded, byte-aligned thumbnails in memory-mapped image tables; 59 vs 35 FPS scrolling on iOS 7-era hardware.
how_it_is_fast: Images of one format are decoded once into uncompressed, correctly aligned bitmaps and stored together in a memory-mapped 'image table' file. Displaying one wraps the mapped bytes in a CGImage that Core Animation can use without copying or decoding, so scrolling does no JPEG work on the main thread.
use_it_when: Maintaining an older app that already uses it for many same-sized thumbnails
skip_it_when: New code: use UIImage.preparingForDisplay() or byPreparingThumbnail(ofSize:) (iOS 15+) or an image loader that decodes off the main thread
Images that do not share a small set of fixed sizes
Disk space matters: the demo used about 4x the disk of the source JPEGs
caveats: Measured in the iOS 7 era (README: 'As of iOS 7'); device not named
A single run of the demo app, with no build configuration stated
Baseline decodes on the main thread; any modern loader that decodes in the background would close much of the gap
tradeoffs: About 4x the disk usage of the compressed images
Every image format must declare fixed pixel dimensions and style up front

evidence.quote: The takeaway is that Fast Image Cache sacrifices disk usage to achieve a faster framerate and overall less memory usage.
As of iOS 7, Apple does not make their hardware JPEG decoder available for third-party applications to use. As a result, only a slower, software decoder is used for this step.
